source_snapshot.test_set: AMD CPU RAS -PCIe Poisoned TLP TX/RX Error
source_snapshot.procedure: Uses fixed 0:0:1/core3/port0 with pcieerror errortype 6 for TX and 7 for RX under ACS/AER, literal severity and SyncFlood settings, but defines no traffic transaction that carries or consumes poison.
source_snapshot.criteria: Calls both errors correctable, accepts tool PASS and OS report within undefined timeout.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; broad log grep cannot prove poison direction, transaction consumption or application/data-path outcome and mixes unrelated PCIe error classes.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: RPUC/CHANGED; adds target/recovery gates but assumes errortype direction/severity and does not specify disposable traffic, requester/completer attribution or deterministic handling.

historical_reviews.deepseek: Cannot show that a Poisoned TLP was transmitted, consumed or attributed to the target.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Improves execution boundaries but tool status plus generic OS evidence cannot distinguish TX and RX data paths.
historical_reviews.related_cases: Rows 57/58 use einjbiopcie errortype 6 for endpoint/root-port nonfatal poison; this row uses pcieerror 6/7 for TX/RX, so command-family semantics cannot be inferred from equal numbers.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Poison validation requires a known disposable transaction, direction roles, source/requester/completer evidence and bounded consumer outcome.

original_test_intent: Verify Poisoned-TLP handling in both transmit and receive directions for every required PCIe slot, proving the poison traverses an approved disposable transaction, is attributed to the intended path and produces the defined correctable/non-fatal consumer outcome without persistent link or data corruption.
original_method: Map each NIC/slot to BDF and NBIO/core/port; obtain authoritative pcieerror 6/7 direction and severity semantics; define transmitter, receiver, requester/completer and a disposable checksum-protected transaction; baseline AER/link/device/process state; inject TX once and correlate the consumed transaction and source; recover fully, then separately inject RX; verify severity, application/I/O outcome, no fatal escalation and restored data/link health; restore BIOS/HDT/AER state.
manual_activity: The FAE maps the path, approves command semantics and a disposable poison-carrying transaction, performs separate TX and RX injections, diagnoses consumer impact and owns driver/link recovery and restoration.
required_inputs: Physical slot/NIC serial/FW/driver/BDF to socket/die/NBIO/core/port map for each target
AMD tool/spec proof that pcieerror errortype 6/7 select Poisoned-TLP TX/RX and their severity
Requester/completer and transmitter/receiver roles plus a disposable bounded transaction that actually carries and consumes poison
Expected AER status/source ID/severity and process/packet/I/O/checksum outcome per direction
Decoded 7EF6030, masks, DPC/SyncFlood policy and correctable-versus-nonfatal decision
Supported OS, timeout, aborts, OOB recovery, RDIMM relevance and restoration
safety_requirements: Dedicated quiesced NIC/link with independent OOB management and no production or persistent data traffic
Verify live tuple and dependency path; use only disposable checksum-protected buffers/packets
Execute TX and RX separately and restore known-good link/device/process state between directions
Abort on wrong source, unexpected data modification, fatal/DPC/SyncFlood escalation, driver reset, link loss or host reset
No automatic retry; preserve evidence and restore/diff BIOS/HDT/AER/SyncFlood and NIC state
agent_execution_scope: Validate command semantics, topology, transaction isolation, direction roles, AER/consumer oracle and recovery plan
Collect read-only PCIe/AER, link/device, traffic/checksum, process/I/O, OS/BMC and post-health evidence
Do not install NIC, choose tuple/transaction/outcome, change BIOS/HDT, inject/reset/rebind/retry/recover or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve per-slot tuple, direction/severity flags and disposable consumer
Approve AER plus application/data-path acceptance matrix
Supervise separate TX/RX stimuli and recovery

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: A generic grep cannot show which transaction carried poison, which side detected it or whether data/application integrity was preserved.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After live topology and flag approval, run separate TX and RX stimuli against an isolated disposable transaction and correlate exact AER source/severity with consumer outcome and recovery.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Tuple 0:0:1/core3/port0, pcieerror errortype 6/7, correctable Criteria, severity/SyncFlood settings, slot 1~N and 30/60-minute values remain preserved but gated.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Execute separate topology-mapped TX/RX poison cases using disposable checksum-protected transactions and prove direction-specific AER plus bounded consumer recovery.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds command-family authority, traffic roles, an actual poison consumer, integrity oracle, per-direction closure and rollback.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Tool PASS and generic OS reporting cannot prove Poisoned-TLP propagation or consumer handling.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Poison may abort or corrupt I/O, terminate a process, reset a device/driver, trip DPC/SyncFlood or disconnect a critical endpoint.

project_override_considerations: If no safe transaction can consume poison for a device class, retain that target as pending rather than injecting without an observable consumer. Do not equate pcieerror 6 with einjbiopcie 6 without vendor documentation.
expected_evidence: Exact NIC/slot/BDF/NBIO path and dependency identity
Tool/spec direction/severity mapping plus decoded AER policy
Disposable transaction, roles, buffer/packet identity and checksum baseline
Separate TX and RX transcripts with exact AER source/status/severity
Consumer/application/I/O outcome and no fatal escalation or persistent link/data impact
Restored state and engineer verdict per direction

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Criteria call Poisoned TLP correctable without defining severity; pcieerror 6/7 TX/RX meanings lack authority and differ from einjbiopcie usage. Slot 1~N uses one tuple, no transaction consumes poison, requester/completer attribution and deterministic outcome are absent, 7EF6030 is undecoded, timeout/RHEL 2022 and RDIMM relevance are ambiguous.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Directional Poisoned-TLP intent is identifiable. Engineering can supply command semantics, safe consumer and oracle, so static review completes while execution stays gated.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row 67 Wistron-System RAS-00787-V002: provide per-slot NIC/BDF-to-NBIO/core/port mapping and vendor proof pcieerror errortype 6/7 mean Poisoned-TLP TX/RX, including relation to einjbiopcie errortype 6; decide correctable/nonfatal severity; define requester/completer roles, isolated poison-consuming transaction, exact AER and process/I/O/checksum outcomes; approve 7EF6030/masks/DPC/SyncFlood, supported OS, timeout, aborts, OOB recovery, RDIMM relevance and restoration.

review_improvement: Introduces the missing poison carrier/consumer and direction-specific integrity oracle, preventing numeric flag assumptions and generic logs from masquerading as end-to-end Poisoned-TLP coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: A poison injection is not demonstrated merely by arming an error bit; an identified transaction must carry the poisoned payload to an observable consumer. TX and RX labels depend on the injection port's perspective and must be reconciled with requester/completer roles. Because errortype 6 appears under another command family with different targeting, the number alone cannot establish identical semantics or severity.
